In commit b043138246a4 (""x86/KVM: Make sure KVM_VCPU_FLUSH_TLB flag is
not missed"") we switched to using a gfn_to_pfn_cache for accessing the
guest steal time structure in order to allow for an atomic xchg of the
preempted field. This has a couple of problems.
Firstly
column2: kvm_map_gfn() doesn't work at all for IOMEM pages when the

column1: atomic flag is set
column2: which it is in kvm_steal_time_set_preempted(). So a

column1: guest vCPU using an IOMEM page for its steal time would never have its
preempted field set.
Secondly
column2: the gfn_to_pfn_cache is not invalidated in all cases where it

column1: should have been. There are two stages to the GFN->PFN conversion;
first the GFN is converted to a userspace HVA
looked up in the process page tables to find the underlying host PFN.
Correct invalidation of the latter would require being hooked up to the
MMU notifiers
column2: but that doesn't happen---so it just keeps mapping and

column1: unmapping the *wrong* PFN after the userspace page tables change.
In the !IOMEM case at least the stale page *is* pinned all the time it's
cached
column2: so it won't be freed and reused by anyone else while still

column1: receiving the steal time updates. The map/unmap dance only takes care
of the KVM administrivia such as marking the page dirty.
Until the gfn_to_pfn cache handles the remapping automatically by
integrating with the MMU notifiers
column2: we might as well not get a

column1: kernel mapping of it
column2: and use the perfectly serviceable userspace HVA

column1: that we already have.  We just need to implement the atomic xchg on
the userspace address with appropriate exception handling
fairly trivial.
